title: Venice
completionText: You leave Venice by water, the bells of San Marco fading behind you. Paris—the final stage—awaits.

cards.dialogue: "The lagoon spreads before you, silver in the morning mist. The bell tower of San Marco rises in the distance, and the Doge's Palace seems to float on the water. Your gondolier asks where to land."
cards.rightChoice: San Marco, at the fashionable inns
cards.leftText: You take rooms above a silk-merchant. The bargaining downstairs is a free education in Venetian commerce.
cards.rightText: The Locanda del Leone Bianco overlooks the piazzetta. A French marquise reads in the next loggia.

cards.dialogue: "Forgive my bauta, signore. In Carnevale even a Senator goes masked. Come, I shall show you a ridotto where the play is high and the company select — though discretion is everything."
cards.leftText: You wander through Piazza San Marco instead, where a Greek vendor sells you good coffee for a single soldo.
cards.rightText: By midnight you have lost twenty zecchini at biribissi. The stranger removes her mask only to laugh.

cards.dialogue: "His Serenity grants audiences to curious foreigners on Wednesdays. The Bucintoro is in dry-dock, alas, but the Sala del Maggior Consiglio alone is worth the silk stockings and the silver."
cards.leftText: You watch the procession of ambassadors from the colonnade. The Doge's robes of cloth-of-gold catch the sun.
cards.rightText: The Doge addresses you in fluent French and recalls his correspondence with Lord Bute. You leave dizzy.

cards.dialogue: "My gondolier tells me you are newly arrived from Rome, signore. I keep a small salon — poets, musicians, the occasional foreign milord. The Abbé Morellet wrote me a sonnet last week. Discretion, naturally, is assured."
cards.leftText: You dine alone at a trattoria off the Frezzeria. The wine is good, the conversation entirely your own.
cards.rightText: The salon is brilliant. You leave with a manuscript of her translations of Pope's Pastorals.

cards.dialogue: "Murano's secrets have been guarded for centuries — on pain of death, signore. But for a worthy visitor, I demonstrate the spinning of a goblet. The price reflects the privilege, you understand."
cards.leftText: You glimpse the furnace's white heart from the threshold. An apprentice scowls and shuts the door.
cards.rightText: The master spins a cristallo goblet thinner than paper. You buy it before it cools.

cards.dialogue: "The Council of Ten notes, signore, that you have asked many questions about the Arsenale. Foreigners who ask such questions sometimes vanish into the Piombi above us — for their own protection, of course. Perhaps your interests lie elsewhere?"
cards.leftText: Your remaining days in Venice are spent firmly inside the picture galleries. Two men in capes follow you to the gondola.
cards.rightText: A night in a damp cell concentrates the mind. By morning a magistrate releases you with apologies and a basket of figs.
